title: Multi-Dimensional and Message-Guided Fuzzing for Robotic Programs in Robot Operating System
problem: Existing fuzzing approaches for ROS programs have inefficient test case generation, ineffective program feedback, and weak generality/automation. There is a lack of targeted fuzzing strategies that understand ROS-specific communication patterns and program structures.
motivation: As robotics applications increasingly rely on ROS, improving the reliability and security of ROS-based programs through more effective automated testing is critical for safe robot deployment.
method: The technique finds bugs in robot programs by systematically testing them with many varied inputs, a process called fuzzing. It does this in two ways: first, by using knowledge of how the Robot Operating System (ROS) sends messages between components to guide which test cases to try (message-guided fuzzing), and second, by exploring many different dimensions of the input space simultaneously (multi-dimensional fuzzing). This approach generates test cases more likely to find bugs and collects richer feedback about how the program responds.
key_novelty: The core contribution is combining multi-dimensional fuzzing with guidance from the Robot Operating System's message-passing patterns to generate better test cases for robot programs.
contributions: Multi-dimensional fuzzing framework tailored to ROS program structure
Message-guided test case generation leveraging ROS message semantics
Improved program feedback collection mechanisms for ROS-based systems
Enhanced generality and automation for robotic program testing
limitations: Not discussed in the provided abstract.
primary_theme: fuzzing and bug detection for ROS programs
